name: Air Recovery: When Not to Recover
summary: Recover in the air - and learn why doing it near the opponent is risky.
description: Recover in the air - and learn why doing it near the opponent is risky.

pages.title: Air Recovery
pages.text: When the juggle gauge empties, hold toward or away from the opponent and press A, B, C, or S to recover in the air. This air recovery is often called a {term:tech}. S is often the safest choice because it is less likely to leave an attack input behind.

pages.title: The Risk
pages.text: After air recovery, you are briefly unable to move, attack, or even block. Recovering close to the opponent can give them a new combo. If you do not recover, you become invulnerable when the juggle expires and fall into a normal knockdown instead.

tasks.label: Recover away from Misaki
tasks.prompt: Misaki will launch you with her {input:236A} projectile. When recovery becomes available, hold away from Misaki and press A, B, C, or S.

feedback.success: You recovered away from Misaki and created more space.
feedback.failure: That recovery moved toward Misaki. Hold away from her before pressing A, B, C, or S.

tasks.label: Recover toward Misaki
tasks.prompt: Let the {input:236A} projectile launch you again. This time, hold toward Misaki and press A, B, C, or S when recovery becomes available.

feedback.success: You recovered toward Misaki. Notice how much closer this leaves you.
feedback.failure: That recovery moved away from Misaki. Hold toward her before pressing A, B, C, or S.

tasks.label: Do not recover once and land safely
tasks.prompt: Let Misaki's {input:236A} projectile launch you - then hands off. Press no recovery direction or button and let Nayuki fall all the way to the ground.

feedback.success: You skipped air recovery and fell into a normal knockdown.
feedback.failure: You recovered before landing. On this attempt, leave the recovery inputs alone.

cue.text: 236A incoming - recover TOWARD Misaki after launch
